text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long your child has been experiencing these nosebleeds and skin spots, and if there's any history of similar issues in the family?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Has your child had any recent infections, fever, or been on any new medications or supplements? Also, does the child have any known allergies or family history of bleeding disorders?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has your child been experiencing any fatigue, bone pain, or unexplained fevers recently, and have you noticed any enlargement of the lymph nodes or liver? Also, does the child have a history of easy bruising from minor bumps?

text: Past medical history: No significant past medical issues. Up-to-date on vaccinations. Social history: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one older sibling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the child have any recent history of viral infections, and have you noticed any swelling of the lymph nodes or spleen? I will also need to see a complete blood count with a peripheral smear to evaluate the platelet levels and cell morphology.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal). Peripheral Blood Smear: No clumping of platelets observed, normal morphology of other cells. Coagulation Profile: PT 12 seconds (normal), aPTT 30 seconds (normal). Special Test (ELISA Binding Assay): Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors.

speaker: Doctor
text: The test results showing normal platelet counts and coagulation profiles, but a deficiency in GIIb/IIIa receptors, are highly specific. This pattern confirms a diagnosis of Glanzmann's Thrombasthenia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann's Thrombasthenia.
